case_source: (From the Judgment and order dated 12th June, 2005 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No.4791 of 1995).
full_judgment:
Md. Abdul Wahhab Miah J. This appeal, by leave, is from the judgment and order dated the 12th day of June, 2005 passed by a learned Judge of the Single Bench of the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 4791 of 1995 making the Rule absolute in part.

<u>2. Facts necessary to dispose this appeal are that the predecessor-in-interest of respondent Nos.1(a)-1(c) herein as the plaintiff filed Title Suit No. 03 of 1986 in the Court of the then Munsif (now the Assistant Judge), Sadar, Gopalgonj for declaration of title to the suit land along with some other declarations stating, inter alia, that 'ka' and 'kha' scheduled land to the plaint belonged to Bireswar Dhali, Malin Chandra Dhali, the plaintiff and Alok Chandra Dhali. Alok Chandra Dhali sold 26½  decimals land from schedules la and 'kha to the plaint by a registered kabala dated 20.02.1954 in favour of the plaintiff. Bireswar Dhali transferred 19½ decimals land from 'ka' scheduled land by a deed of gift dated 03.09.1984 in favour of the plaintiff. The S.A record was wrongly recorded in the name of Laxmimoni, the mother of Bireswar along with others. The said entry of Laxmimoni in the S.A. record was wrong. Alok Chandra by his transfer vide the sale, deed dated 20.02.1954 exhausted his share in the suit land. The S.A record was also prepared in the name of Alok Chandra wrongly. Defendant No.1 created two kabalas from the sons of Alok Chandra Dhali and demanded title in the suit land for the first time on 06.11.1985, on the basis of the said kabala; hence the suit.</u>

3. The trial Court dismissed the suit (the date of the decree is not available from the record). Against the judgment and decree of the trial Court, the plaintiff filed Title Appeal No.15 of 1991 before the District Judge, Gopalgonj. The Appellate Court allowed the appeal and sent the suit on remand to the trial Court with observation that the plaintiff ought to have filed the suit for declaration of title and partition by impleading the necessary parties in the, suit. After remand the plaintiff amended the plaint and added the prayer for confirmation of possession and for partition.

4. The suit was contested by defendant No.1 by filing a written statement contending, inter alia, that Alok Chandra and Bireswar did not transfer any land to the plaintiff by the kabalas dated 20.02.1984 and 03.09.1984 respectively. Alok Chandra Dhali and Bireswar Dhali had migrated to India 25/30 years before and they died there but the plaintiff created the false deeds of transfer in their names. The defendant purchased the suit land from the heirs of Alok Dhali and Bireswar by the three kabalas and he has been in possession thereof by mutating his name and paying rents to the government. The plaintiff had no title and possession in the suit, so they had no cause of action to file the suit and the suit was liable to be dismissed.

5. After amendment P.W 1 was recalled and he was examined. The trial Court by the judgment and decree dated 25.06.2002 decreed the suit in part declaring title of the plaintiff in respect of 06½ 2 decimal land in Plot No.2469 of R.S Khatian No. 606 and also giving saham for the said area of the land. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the judgment and decree of the trial Court, the plaintiff filed Title Appeal No. 69 of 1995 before the District Judge, Gopalgonj. The learned Subordinate Judge, 1st Court, Gopalgonj by his judgment and decree dated 28.09.1995 dismissed the appeal and at the same time dismissed the suit. Against the judgment and decree of the Appellate Court, the plaintiff filed Civil Revision No. 47 of 1985 before the High Court Division. A learned Judge of the Single Bench by the impugned judgment and order made the Rule absolute, set aside the judgment and decree of the Appellate Court and decreed the suit in part confirming plaintiff's title and possession in 59 decimals land in schedule 'ka' and 13 decimals land in schedule 'kha' to the plaint, but dismissed the prayer for partition for "non joinder of parties and property." The learned Judge further observed that "However, the plaintiff may file a fresh suit for partition impleading the Roads and High Way and on bringing the entire land of schedule 'ka ' and Kha to the plaint in the 'said suit."

6. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the judgment and order of the High Court Division, the defendant-appellant filed Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 1160 of 2005 before this Court and leave was granted giving rise to this appeal to consider the submissions made on his behalf to the following effect:

"Mr. Md. Shamsul Huda, learned Advocate, appearing for the petitioner submits that the High Court Division committed error of law in reversing the concurrent finding of facts made by the Courts below that the plaintiff has failed to prove his right, title, interest and possession over suit land, particularly the land described in 'ka' schedule of the plaint without controverting the above finding with reference to evidence on record, confirming the title and possession of the plaintiff over 59 decimal of land from 'ka' schedule that is in Plot No. 2469 of R.S Khatian No. 603 of the aforesaid Mauza. Although the plaintiff filed the instant suit for .20 decimals of land of 'ka' schedule of the plaint and 6½ decimals from 'kha' schedule land of the plaint and the above finding of the High Court is beyond the pleading.".

7. Mr. Nurul Amin, learned Counsel for the appellant, has firstly pointed out that in the suit, the plaintiff did not examine himself and on his behalf his son was examined as P.W1 without having any authority from him (the plaintiff). Therefore, in the absence of any evidence of the plaintiff, there was only pleading and pleading could not be basis for decreeing a suit. He has further contended that the High Court Division itself found that the suit for partition was not maintainable because the necessary party, namely, Roads and Highway, in whose favour a portion of suit plot was acquired, was not impleaded as a defendant and that the entire properties of the khatian were not brought in hotchpotch, it erred in law in decreeing the suit confirming title and possession in favour of the plaintiff in respect of 59+13 decimals land from the two schedules. He has also contended that suit land was vague as the same was not described as per the mandate of Order VII, ride 3 of the Code of Civil Procedure; the plaintiff was not entitled to the declaration of title and confirmation of possession. He has lastly contended that both the Courts below on discussion of the evidence, found possession of the defendant in the suit land. The proper suit which ought to have been filed by the plaintiff was the suit for partition, but the High Court Division having found the suit for partition non maintainable due to non impleading of the necessary parties and for non inclusion of the entire properties of the khatain in hotchpotch committed a serious error of law in giving declaration of title of the plaintiff to the extent of 59+13 decimals land from the two schedules and as such, the impugned judgment and order be set aside and the appeal be allowed.

8. Mr. Bivash Chandra Biswas, learned Advocate-on-Record for the respondent, on the other hand, has supported the impugned judgment and order. He has submitted that the defendant failed to prove his title in the suit land on the basis of his purchase from the son of Bireswar and Alok Dhali. He has further submitted that the plaintiffs kabala is of the year 1964, whereas, those of the defendant were of the year 1966. Therefore, the High Court Division did not commit any error of law in decreeing the suit finding title of the plaintiff in 59+13 decimals land and there being no merit in the appeal, the same be dismissed.

9. We have considered the submissions of the learned Counsel as well as the learned Advocate-on-Record of the respective party and we have gone through the materials on record. Admittedly initially the suit was filed only for declaration of title along with the other declarations that the kabalas dated 03.06.1985 being Nos. 498 and 4199 of the Office of Sub-Registrar, Gopalgonj in favour of defendant No.1 showing Modhusudan as its executor were fraudulent, collusive, illegal, null and void, inoperative; and was not binding' upon the plaintiff and the S.A khatians being Nos. 260 and 72 in the name of Alek Dhaki as described in the schedule to the plaint was fraudulent, collusive; illegal, null and void and not binding upon the plaintiff. The suit was dismissed and on appeal, the Appellate Court sent the suit on remand to the trial Court with the following observations;

"উক্তরূপে উচিৎ এবং যথাযথ ব্যক্তিদেরকে পক্ষ করতঃ স্বত্ব সাব্যস্ত পূর্বক বাটোয়ারার প্রার্থনাসহ আনুষাঙ্গিক প্রতিকারের মোকদ্দমায় পক্ষদ্বয়ের বিবাদমান বিষয়ে নিষ্পত্তি উপযুক্ত মোকদ্দমা বলিয়া মনে করি। সুতরাং তর্কিত পর্যালোচনা ও তন্মুরে উপনীত সিদ্ধান্ত তথা রায় ও ডিক্রী আইন ও ঘটনাগত দিক হইতে সঠিক ও যুক্তিযুক্ত না  হওয়ায় তাহা বহালযোগ্য নহে রদরহিতযোগ্য হইতেছে এবং মূল মোকদ্দমাটি উপরোক্ত পর্যালোচনার আলোকে পুনঃ বিচারের নিমিত্তে বিজ্ঞ নিম্ন আদালতে প্রেরণের যোগ্য হইতেছে। অত্র বিবেচ্য বিষয়ের সিন্ধান্ত অত্ররুপে নিস্পত্তি হয়। ফলতঃ অত্র আপীল মোকদ্দমাটি কৃতকার্য্য হইয়াছে। "

10. From the above quoted observation made by the Appellate Court, it is clear that though the plaintiff amended the plaint adding the prayer for partition and also made amendment in the schedule to the plaint, he did not implead the necessary parties and also did not bring all the properties in hotchpotch. From the impugned judgment, it appears that the High Court Division itself gave finding in clear language that in view of the fact that necessary parties were not impleaded in the suit and all the properties were not brought in hotchpotch, the suit for partition was not maintainable, yet decreed the suit only in respect the prayer for title of the plaintiff. From the evidence, it appears that some of the P.Ws admitted the possession of defendant No. 1 in the suit land. The High Court Division did not reverse the finding of possession given by the Courts below with reference to the evidence on record. It further appears that the High Court Division gave abrupt finding that the plaintiff was in possession in the suit and that the defendant was not in possession thereof.

11. We have not been able to lay our hand on any provision of law either in the Code of Civil Procedure or any other law that when the plaintiff(s) makes the prayer for declaration of title, confirmation of possession and for partition, the Court can suo moto split up the prayers and give the relief to the plaintiff(s) for declaration in respect of the property which was subsequently included in the schedule to the plaint for partition. It is a fact that the plaintiff is in possession in the homestead property of plot No. 2469 and it is also in evidence that the defendant is in possession in a portion of the suit land.

<u>12. In view of the above, we are of the view that justice would be best served to both the parties if the appeal is remanded to the Appellate Court for hearing afresh giving chance to the plaintiff to amend the plaint by impleading the necessary party, namely, Roads and Highway and the other necessary parties, if there be any and also bringing in hotchpotch the entire property of the khatian. In the context, we would observe that under section 107, of the Code of Civil Procedure, the Appellate Court is clothed with all the powers of a trial Court. The plaintiff is directed to make the necessary amendment in the plaint within 2 (two) months from the date of receipt of this judgment, failing which the suit shall stand dismissed.</u>

13. In view of the fact that we are sending the appeal back to the Appellate Court for hearing it afresh, we refrain ourselves from making any comment about the first point raised by Mr. Nurul Amin as noted hereinbefore. However, the Appellate Court will decide the point along with the other issues. The parties are directed to maintain status-quo in respect of the position and the possession of the suit land till disposal of the appeal.

14. Accordingly, the impugned judgment and order is set aside. The appeal is sent back to the Appellate Court for hearing it afresh and for disposal in accordance with law in the, light of the observation made and the finding given hereinbefore.

15. With above observation, finding, and the direction, this appeal is disposed of.

End.
